correctness.rationale: The forbidden-simple-edge union of two perfect matchings is a disjoint union of simple even cycles for superposition parts >=2, and isolated ordinary edges for parts 1. Its matching polynomial enumerates exactly the sets used in the inclusion-exclusion formula for their common-neighbour count. The cyclic two-state transfer matrix has determinant -z and gives \(C_{2m}(z)^2-C_{4m}(z)=2z^{2m}\). Multiplying by a residual matching polynomial and shifting the index by the even exponent gives exactly twice the residual common-neighbour count. The residual is zero only for a single forbidden edge: the empty case counts one matching, the four-vertex cases are explicit, and for at least six vertices the complement has minimum degree at least half its order and therefore has a perfect matching. For odd \(n\ge5\) both relevant graph vertices are nonneighbours of the singleton anchor, their common-neighbour counts are equal, and regularity forces identical second-round colours. Their full automorphism orbits differ by their cycle types, using Godsil-Meagher Lemma 10.1. Standalone exact-integer programs verify finite cases through distinct constructions; they are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural symmetric family with nontrivial perfect-matching association scheme exhibits an exact local-statistic switch law. The quantified zero classification pinpoints a genuine infinite two-round orbit recovery obstruction when the residual superposition consists of one shared edge. This explains a structural parity phenomenon for finite counting refinement and is not simply a small-case observation, rename of a known bound, or an arbitrary finite computation. It does not depend on an unproved all-rank stabilization conjecture.
